name: Jerry Rice
headline: The standard for every receiver.
bio: Rice combined precise routes with extraordinary longevity across a 20-season career. His receiving totals remain landmarks for every future generation.

name: Walter Payton
headline: Sweetness. Strength. Staying power.
bio: Payton powered Chicago with a blend of balance, durability and all-purpose skill. His impact reached beyond rushing to receiving, blocking and leadership.

name: Lawrence Taylor
headline: The edge that changed the game.
achievements: 3× NFL Defensive Player of the Year
bio: Taylor forced offenses to rethink protection. His speed and power helped turn the outside linebacker into an attacking focal point. Sack total covers the official-stat era from 1982.

name: Joe Montana
headline: Calm when the stakes were highest.
bio: Montana directed a precise passing attack and delivered memorable late-game drives. His career linked the rise of the West Coast offense with championship execution.

name: Emmitt Smith
headline: The long road to the rushing summit.
bio: Smith supplied sustained production at the heart of the Dallas dynasty. His patience, vision and durability carried him to the top of the career rushing record book.

name: Jim Brown
headline: Nine seasons. An enduring benchmark.
bio: Brown dominated an era with power and acceleration. He left football after nine seasons with rushing records that set the target for the runners who followed.

name: Peyton Manning
headline: A master of the line of scrimmage.
bio: Manning made pre-snap command a defining part of quarterback play. He led championship teams in Indianapolis and Denver over an 18-season playing career.

name: Barry Sanders
headline: A cut could change everything.
bio: Sanders turned balance and sudden changes of direction into an unmistakable style. He rushed for at least 1,000 yards in every season of his ten-year career.

name: Reggie White
headline: Power at the point of attack.
bio: White combined strength with refined pass-rush technique. He anchored formidable fronts in Philadelphia and Green Bay and helped the Packers return to a championship.

name: Bill Walsh
headline: An idea became an offensive language.
bio: Walsh built a championship program through teaching, player evaluation and a structured passing system. His coaching influence extended through generations of assistants.

name: John Madden
headline: A teacher who brought football closer.
bio: Madden led consistently successful Raiders teams before becoming a defining football broadcaster. His teaching connected the detail of the game with a broad audience.

name: Don Shula
headline: Consistency measured in decades.
bio: Shula built winning teams across changing eras. His Miami program delivered consecutive championships and the unbeaten 1972 season.

name: George Halas
headline: At the foundations of the league.
bio: Halas helped establish the league and the franchise that became the Chicago Bears. His career spanned playing, coaching, ownership and football administration.
